answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by making every identity carry a bond of locked, slashable stake tied to a public behavioral history. Peers attest independently, acting like a prism that splits one claim into many angles instead of a single measure. Fake accounts that echo each other only reproduce the same weak claim, so consensus never forms, and a raven account copying the herd gains nothing. Faking a thousand voices therefore costs real capital at risk, not free signups.
